title: Minneapolis, his father's big band, and Lester practicing Trumbauer records
summary: The family settled in Minneapolis where his father formed a 13-piece band; Lee sang and Lester practiced constantly to Frankie Trumbauer records.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: at all -- but he wouldn't be judged on his personality; he would be judged on what he was doing with his feet, so, you know, I think that phase of it was very, very interesting -- but I used to dance and sing all the time, you know, on the TOBA circuit, and after we left the TOBA circuit, we moved to Minnesota -- to Minneapolis, and I was going to grammar school. But that's when my dad formed a band in Minneapolis. And, as a matter of fact, the Pettifords were also from Minneapolis because Lester used to hang out with them, you know, and I think we had like a 13-piece band, and many good musicians, but I quit traveling with them during school. I used to sing; I used to be the vocalist in the band, so during school, I would remain in Minneapolis, and then my dad and Lester and them would go out on the road.

But I don't think you ever heard a musician practice more or diligently than Lester did. At that time when we were in Minneapolis, you know, he was a young guy, because I was in grammar school, and his idol at the time was Frankie Trumbauer. A lot of people may not realize it, but he was around when Lester played alto.

And he used to play all of these Frankie Trumbauer records in his room, and I used to hear -- Frankie Trumbauer used to make a lot of records that was -- well, he was running over the horn, and all along, you know? It was like The Bouncing Ball that had funny titles like that. It just showed the dexterity and

his execution, more or less. But the guy used to practice all the time. Now ... from Minneapolis, like, on the way out here, when we stopped in Albuquerque, why, that's when I decided I wanted to play trombone.
